comments.author: nirname
comments.body:
It seems to me that this rule support unbalanced constructions. See the chain of derivations:
```
parseLineData
SQUARE_BRACES_START NUMBER_WITH_DECIMAL parseLineData
SQUARE_BRACES_START NUMBER_WITH_DECIMAL SQUARE_BRACES_START NUMBER_WITH_DECIMAL parseLineData
SQUARE_BRACES_START NUMBER_WITH_DECIMAL SQUARE_BRACES_START NUMBER_WITH_DECIMAL SQUARE_BRACES_END
```
So as to be more clear:
```
parseLineData
[ 10 parseLineData
[ 10 [ 20 parseLineData
[ 10 [ 20 ]
```

You should split the rule so that the internal list of values would be separated from brackets:
```
lineData: "[" listOfValues "]" ;
listOfValues: NUMBER_WITH_DECIMAL | NUMBER_WITH_DECIMAL "," listOfValues
```
Or something similar

Perhaps, this was the reason why you needed the trick with `data_inner` (not sure, though).
comments.label_reasoning: The grammar rule supports unbalanced bracket constructions due to incorrect recursive structure.

comments.author: nirname
comments.body:
1. The same problem of unbalanced brackets.
2. This construction repeats `parseLineData`, so both of them `parseLineData` and  `parseBarData` can be combined into one non-term called `data` (or any other, name choices is up to you)
    e.g
    ```
    statement
      : LINE data
      : BAR data
      ;
    data: "[" values "]";
    values: value | "," values | ;
    ```
    If you want values not to be empty:
    ```
    values: value values_list;
    values_list: "," value | values_list | ;
    ```
    Furthermore, the fact that you are [starting the same directive](https://github.com/mermaid-js/mermaid/pull/4413/files#diff-532cbb4afcc95e6caafa23852a6a0edbf55849150d219ec1bb9f11fe763afef6R52-R53) called `data` for `LINE` and `BAR` only emphasizes the assumption that the latter tho must be combined.
comments.label_reasoning: Same unbalanced bracket issue as in `parseLineData`; also duplicate rules for LINE and BAR data should be combined.

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: Identifies unbalanced bracket bug and suggests combining duplicate rules.

comments.author: nirname

You can give them custom aliases should you need to:
```
text NUMBER_WITH_DECIMAL\[first] ARROW_DELIMITER NUMBER_WITH_DECIMAL\[second]
{yy.setXAxisTitle($text); yy.setXAxisRangeData(Number($first), Number($second));}
```
But they are also [auto-numbered](https://gerhobbelt.github.io/jison/docs/#auto-numbered-named-accessors):
```
{yy.setXAxisTitle($text); yy.setXAxisRangeData(Number($NUMBER_WITH_DECIMAL1), Number($$NUMBER_WITH_DECIMAL2));}
```
comments.label_reasoning: Using positional `$1`, `$2` instead of named or auto-numbered aliases reduces readability.

comments.author: nirname
comments.body:
It seems, than PUNCTUATION unites the majority of previous symbols. But it will never be recognized because of the lexems order. There are 2 options, I think:
* either remove `PUNCTUATION`, and remove it from `alphaNumToken` as well, and leave all of those separate tokens, thus we would get much nicer and clearer parsing error message if any
* or leave PUNCTUATION only, since it already includes everything else
comments.label_reasoning: PUNCTUATION token will never be matched due to lexer ordering; earlier tokens shadow it, making it unreachable.
